title: Onramp SDK: concise streaming + tool contracts with TS/Python/Go samples
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a small set of language idiomatic examples and a compact compatibility shim that demonstrates: 1) progressive token/structured-event streaming, 2) first-class tool/function calling with typed inputs/outputs, and 3) a minimal adapter layer so older SDKs can interoperate with the new streaming+tools envelopes. This ticket is focused on developer experience: small, copy-paste examples for TypeScript, Python, and Go, plus a short compatibility shim design that teams can adopt.
acceptance_criteria: Three language-specific examples (TS, Python, Go) that show: initializing client, streaming generation that emits mixed token and structured events, invoking a tool via function-call envelope, and handling tool responses.
A compatibility shim spec (newline-delimited JSON framing + version header) with a reference TS implementation and integration test proving backward compatibility with older non-streaming clients.
One GitHub PR that adds the examples under docs/sdk-examples/onramp/ and a small test harness that verifies streaming & tool call roundtrip in CI.
Security review notes captured and KMS usage verified for tool payloads containing secrets.
Performance smoke test demonstrating negligible additional latency (<5ms median) from the shim in typical requests for our hosted tier.
steps: Draft compact streaming envelope specification (single-line JSON framing with 'v' version field and 't' type field)
Design typed tool call envelope: {invocation_id, tool_name, input_schema_version, payload}
Implement TS example: onramp/ts/example.ts showing event parsing loop and typed tool registry
Implement Python example: onramp/py/example.py using async generator pattern and schema-validated tool responses
Implement Go example: onramp/go/example.go with channel-based streaming reader and minimal codec
Build compatibility shim in TypeScript (reference): reads new envelope and emits legacy token stream for older SDKs
Add integration tests that spin up a local runtime test harness and assert structured events and tool call roundtrip
Open PR, iterate on reviewer feedback, and land docs + examples
decisions: Use newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) framing with a lightweight 2-field header ('v' and 't') to minimize parser complexity across languages.
Structured events will be typed with a small 'event_type' enum: 'token', 'structured', 'tool_call', 'tool_result', 'done'.
Tool calling will use a separate 'invocation_id' to permit interleaved streaming from multiple invocations in the same session.
Compatibility shim will be adapter-only (no protocol changes on server) and implemented as a small client-side package rather than server middleware.
Pick JSON Schema draft-07 for tool input/output validation to maximize existing library support across TS/Python/Go.
Backpressure: the SDK will expose a simple buffered iterator with a configurable max_inflight_tokens parameter; runtime will maintain sane defaults.
risks: Potential for subtle breaking behavior if older clients parse structured events as tokens; mitigated by strict 't' header and version check in shim.
Increased SDK surface area could add maintenance burden (three languages) - limit internal helpers and keep examples minimal.
Tool payloads may contain secrets: ensure KMS integration and audit logging path is documented and required for production tool connectors.
Parsing errors in streaming can be noisy; propose a best-effort skip-on-error strategy with telemetry to capture frequency.
